rejected.title: Gods and the Olympic Games
card: The ancient Greeks were polytheistic, which means they worshipped many gods. Zeus was the leader of the gods, and each other god had their own area, such as Athena for wisdom and Poseidon for the sea.
Greeks built temples and made offerings to win the gods' favour. They believed the gods affected daily life, such as war, harvests and voyages.
An oracle was a holy place where a priest or priestess passed on a god's answer to a question. People, and even city-states, asked oracles for advice before big decisions.
The Olympic Games were held at Olympia every four years in honour of Zeus. Athletes from many city-states took part, and the Games were a religious festival as well as a sports contest.
rejected.remember: The Greeks honoured many gods, and the Olympic Games were a festival for Zeus.

a.q: The ancient Olympic Games were a religious festival as well as a sports contest. Who were they held to honour?
opts: Zeus, the leader of the gods
Poseidon, the god of the sea
Athena, the goddess of wisdom
The champion athletes of the past
a.why: The Games at Olympia were held every four years in honour of Zeus, the leader of the gods. Athena and Poseidon were important Greek gods too, but each had their own area, and the Games were not held for them.
a.clue: Think about which god led all the others.

b.q: The leaders of a Greek city-state are unsure whether to go to war. They send a messenger to a holy place to get a god's answer. What are they doing?
opts: Consulting an oracle
Holding the Olympic Games
Voting in an assembly
Making an offering at a temple
b.why: An oracle was a holy place where a priest or priestess passed on a god's answer to a question. Making an offering at a temple is tempting, but offerings were meant to win a god's favour, not to get advice.
b.clue: Which practice gave people a god's answer to a question?
